answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy works like a grove at dawn: every new identity starts as a single sapling with limited trust and must earn standing through attested work over time, the way roots deepen season after season. Reputation accrues to one continuous record, so spawning a hundred fresh identities means tending a hundred separate groves from scratch — expensive, slow, and easy to spot — while honest agents keep their cheap, verifiable history, and no shallow lagoon of quick rewards tempts them to abandon it.
